name: routine.run
description: Advisory check before a scheduled routine or weekly automation is called done. The schedule must be named, a dry run must not write, a Flash model must not carry the job, and a new or changed routine must have been rehearsed on a case with a known-good answer before anything was scheduled.

named_schedule.instructions: The artifact names the schedule: a cadence, a next run time, or a routine id. Words like regularly or soon do not count.

writes_only_when_applied.instructions: The refresh script writes catalogs only when the command includes --apply.

carrier_is_not_flash.instructions: The routine carrier is not a Flash model. Blackwell Flash, MiMo Flash, Gemini Flash, and any model id containing flash fail this.

evidence.instructions: How much proof is attached that the last run did what it claims.
criteria: A claim with no command output
A log line that names the mode but not the result
A log that shows dry-run or apply and the exit code
Log plus the files the run was allowed to touch
Log, touched files, and a stated next run time

owner.instructions: The artifact does not propose spend, a send, a push, or a model-id change.

rehearsed_on_known_case.instructions: For a NEW or CHANGED routine, skill, or automation, the artifact shows it was run at least once against a case whose correct answer was already known (the owner's walkthrough case, a prior hand-run, or a fixture with a verified result), and the output was compared to that known answer. 'Should work', 'looks right', a config read-back, or a dry run with no expected-output comparison does not count. An UNCHANGED routine already in service does not need this.

rules.reason: a dry run must not write catalogs
Flash must not carry the routine
owner has to approve a new outward action
a new or changed automation was scheduled without reproducing a known-good result first

notes.bar: Pass line is above 0.9. A noul of 0.90 fails the rule `noul <= 0.90`; 0.91 or higher passes. Score and choice confidence use `confidence <= 0.90`. A score is a mean on levels 0..5, so above 0.9 of that scale is a mean above 4.50.
notes.rehearsal: Added 2026-10-06 from Anthropic's small-business build-agent (Apache 2.0, anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins): 'Run the new skill against a case the owner already knows the answer to... An owner who has seen it reproduce a known-good result will schedule it. One who hasn't will run it manually and check it every time.' ESCALATE rather than BLOCK on purpose: a missed rehearsal is unverifiable trust, not a forbidden action. Companion doctrine: skill-library/skill-release-gate.
